reference\hall\hall-refunds.md:20:2.5 The £30 booking deposit is non-refundable in every hirer cancellation.
reference\hall\hall-refunds.md:21:2.6 Refunds under 2.1 and 2.2 exclude the booking deposit.
reference\hall\hall-refunds.md:30:## 4. Damage deposits
reference\hall\hall-refunds.md:31:4.1 Damage deposits are returned within ten working days after the event.
reference\hall\hall-refunds.md:35:4.5 An unused damage deposit is returned in full after hirer cancellation.
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:4:covers: "Room hire charges, equipment fees, deposits and payment deadlines"
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:36:## 5. Deposits
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:37:5.1 Every booking requires a £30 booking deposit.
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:38:5.2 Parties serving alcohol require a £100 damage deposit.
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:39:5.3 The damage deposit is separate from the booking deposit.
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:40:5.4 The booking deposit counts towards the total hire charge.
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:41:5.5 Damage deposit returns follow hall-refunds.md section 4.
reference\hall\hall-fees.md:44:6.1 The booking deposit is due within seven calendar days of acceptance.
reference\hall\hall-conduct.md:4:covers: "Behaviour, alcohol, noise, cleaning and responsibility for damage"
reference\hall\hall-conduct.md:22:## 3. Alcohol
reference\hall\hall-conduct.md:23:3.1 Alcohol may be served only with prior written permission.
reference\hall\hall-conduct.md:24:3.2 Alcohol may not be sold under an ordinary hall booking.
reference\hall\hall-conduct.md:25:3.3 Permission to serve alcohol requires the damage deposit in hall-fees.md.
reference\hall\hall-conduct.md:26:3.4 The hirer must ensure alcohol is not supplied to underage guests.
reference\hall\hall-conduct.md:27:3.5 Alcohol must not be taken outside the designated hall grounds.
reference\hall\hall-changes.md:47:6.4 The separate booking deposit exclusion still applies.
reference\hall\hall-bookings.md:21:2.6 Failure to pay the booking deposit cancels an accepted booking.

content.text:
The £30 booking deposit is not enough. The hirer needs prior written permission to serve alcohol, and a separate £100 damage deposit. That makes **£130** in deposits altogether.

- **Permission:** Alcohol may be served only with prior written permission (hall-conduct.md, section 3.1). Serving without selling is consistent with section 3.2, which bars selling alcohol under an ordinary booking.
- **Damage deposit:** Parties serving alcohol require a £100 damage deposit (hall-fees.md, section 5.2). Permission to serve alcohol requires this deposit (hall-conduct.md, section 3.3).
- **Booking deposit:** Every booking requires the £30 booking deposit (hall-fees.md, section 5.1). The damage deposit is separate from it (section 5.3).

hall-changes.md does not replace any of these sections.
